items.title: Weak unramifiedness is preserved by a totally ramified separable base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an extension A -> B of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields K in L, assumes A -> B weakly unramified, and asserts that for any finite separable extension K_1/K totally ramified with respect to A one has that L_1 = L tensor_K K_1 is a field, that A_1 and B_1 = B tensor_A A_1 are discrete valuation rings, and that the extension A_1 in B_1 is weakly unramified (source lines 34489-34498). The proof works with uniformizers and the minimal polynomial. Writing pi in A and pi_1 in A_1 for uniformizers, total ramifiedness gives pi_1^e = u_1 pi for a unit u_1 of A_1, so that A_1 is generated over A by pi_1 and the minimal polynomial P(t) of pi_1 over K has the displayed Eisenstein shape t^e + a_{e-1} t^{e-1} + ... + a_0 with all a_i in (pi) and a_0 = u pi for a unit u of A (proof lines 34501-34509). The proof records that e = [K_1 : K] (proof line 34510). The substantive step is the base change: since A -> B is weakly unramified, pi is a uniformizer of B, so B_1 = B[t]/(P(t)) is a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer the class of t, from which all three assertions follow (proof lines 34510-34513). The non-routine content is the reduction of the weak unramifiedness of the base change to the statement that B[t]/(P(t)) is a discrete valuation ring with the evident uniformizer.
